GoFull

Development of a Mobile App for Fuel Delivery and Car Towing

Student: Ahmed Ahmeid (3965)
Supervisor: Mrs. Hanein Omar Mohamed Shareif Hassan
02
The Problem

A Dual Market Failure on Libya's Roads

Driver Pain

Fuel runs out or the car breaks down — in a remote area or late at night — and there is no organized way to get help: informal networks, phone calls and social-media posts mean safety risks, opaque pricing and long delays.

Provider Pain

Fuel delivery agents and tow truck operators cannot reach customers efficiently — no unified platform, difficulty finding a customer's exact location, lost income and poor coordination.

03
The Solution

Introducing GoFull

An on-demand roadside assistance platform connecting stranded drivers directly with nearby fuel delivery agents and tow truck operators.

Speed & Safety

Request help in a few taps — the request reaches approved providers within 30 km, nearest first, emergencies first.

Trust & Transparency

Document-verified providers, OTP-secured accounts, two-way ratings and prices computed by the server.

Live Tracking

GPS-based location detection and a live map of the provider approaching, with one-tap phone contact.

04
Engineering Process

Project Methodology

The Waterfall Model was adopted to ensure a logical, sequential progression — each phase completed and documented before the next begins.

1. Requirements
Feasibility study, SRS, 15 use cases & 14 features for all three actors
2. Design
UML models: activity, sequence, class, ERD, component & deployment diagrams
3. Implementation
Flutter mobile app · Laravel REST API · Blade admin dashboard
4. Testing
API, functional, integration & regression testing — 16 traced test cases
5. Deployment
Deployed to a live testing environment for evaluation on real devices
05
Project Boundaries

Scope & Limitations

In Scope

  • Mobile App (Drivers): register & authenticate, set live GPS location, request fuel بنزين or towing ساحبة, get matched to the nearest available provider, track and rate.
  • Provider Mode: receive nearby requests, accept, navigate to the driver, update status, view earnings & history.
  • Admin Dashboard: manage customers & providers, verify accounts, monitor real-time activity, review requests and analyze performance.

Limitations

  • No online payment in the initial version — cash on delivery only.
  • Requires internet & GPS access at all times.
  • Limited service coverage during the early launch phase.
06
Validation

Feasibility Study

Operational

A survey of 23 potential users (22 drivers, 1 provider) confirms a clear market need on both sides of the platform.

Technical

One Flutter app for both roles + a Laravel backend — modern, open-source, no proprietary hardware.

Legal

Complies with Libyan Law No. (10) of 2010 on Electronic Transactions; cash-only avoids FinTech licensing.

09
Core Domain

The Service Request Lifecycle

Every request moves through a forward-only status chain — enforced by the server, never trusted to the client.

pending
offered to providers ≤ 30 km
accepted
race-safe atomic claim
en_route
live GPS streams to the driver
arrived
at the stranded car
in_progress
refueling / towing + photo log
completed
cash collected, both sides rate

Forward-only validation

Backward moves are rejected; skipped steps (flaky networks) are allowed with automatic timestamp backfill.

Race-safe accept

A conditional UPDATE inside a transaction — two providers can never claim the same request.

Auto-expiry

A scheduler cancels unaccepted requests every minute — 15 min normal, 10 min emergency.

10
Implementation

Software Architecture & Design Patterns

Backend (Laravel): MVC

  • Models: 12 Eloquent models with relationships & casts
  • Controllers: separate Driver, Provider & Admin namespaces
  • FormRequests validate every input; Services hold OTP & notification logic
  • Events broadcast state changes; transactions keep writes atomic

Mobile (Flutter): Clean Architecture + BLoC

  • Presentation: screens + widgets driven by 6 Blocs & 3 Cubits
  • Domain: entities + 22 use-cases returning Either<Failure, T>
  • Data: Dio datasources + repository implementations
  • Feature-first folders, wired by GetIt (44 registrations)

15
Looking Ahead

Limitations & Future Work

Current Limitations

  • Cash on delivery only — no online payment.
  • Requires continuous internet and GPS connectivity.
  • Limited coverage during the early launch phase.

Future Roadmap

  • Online payment gateways and a digital wallet once regulation allows.
  • More roadside services — battery jump-start, tyre change.
  • Graceful offline handling and extended language support.
  • Richer provider analytics with trends and forecasting.
16
Summary

Conclusion

All Objectives Achieved

A full SRS with 15 use cases and 14 features, a complete UML design, and a working client–server platform — specified, designed, implemented and tested.

Technical Achievement

Two apps from one Flutter codebase, a hand-built real-time layer over Laravel Reverb, and a server-enforced lifecycle that survives races, restarts and flaky networks.

Final Verdict

Verified through API, functional, integration and regression testing — a deployment-ready platform that modernizes roadside assistance in Libya.
